    • Recent findings suggest that we got our first technical deep dive into AMD's next-generation Zen 6 CPU architecture last week, in the form of the company's upcoming Venice range of server chips.
    • In a recent development, the latest Ryzen offerings were originally thought to be launching in the first half, but Chiphell leaker Zhang Zhonghao says otherwise.
    • Zhang Zhonghao makes mention of Computex in their post, which some are speculating means a launch date after the show in June of next year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that we got our first technical deep dive into AMD's next-generation Zen 6 CPU architecture last week, in the form of the company's upcoming Venice range of server chips. Now there's a rumour that the consumer Ryzen chip launch may have been pushed back to the second half of 2027.

    In a recent development, the latest Ryzen offerings were originally thought to be launching in the first half, but Chiphell leaker Zhang Zhonghao says otherwise. In a post spotted by Videocardz, Zhang Zhonghao claims that the desktop chips, codenamed Olympic Ridge, have been switched to TSMC's N2X manufacturing process, and as a result the "timeline has been pushed back" (via machine translation).

    Zhang Zhonghao makes mention of Computex in their post, which some are speculating means a launch date after the show in June of next year.

    Olympic Ridge was originally though to be using TSMC's N2 or N2P process node, but a switch to the performance-focussed N2X would line up with previous rumours that the chips are targeting very high clockspeeds, potentially all the way up to 6.5 GHz.

    It has been revealed that N2X is scheduled to enter production in 2027, which would explain the longer timeframe if this rumour proves out. A delay to the second half of next year would mean that Intel's Nova Lake chips, said by the company to be "tracking ahead of schedule" in a recent earnings call, would potentially have the first half of 2026 all to themselves if they launch before Zen 6.

    Sources indicate that in the battle of the next generation CPUs, Intel would end up with a significant headstart. However, for those thinking about a potential upgrade, it's worth noting that Intel's new chips will use an entirely new socket in the form of LGA 1954. AMD's new offerings will use the existing AM5 socket.

    AMD's Jack Huynh posted a cryptic video on X earlier this week, alongside a message declaring that "the next era of computing is going to be special," and that he "can't wait to share a glimpse of what's coming at CES." So, hopefully we might learn more about what's going on with Zen 6 desktop silicon on January 5.

    The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

    3. Best RAM: G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB 32 GB DDR5-7200.

    It has been revealed that 5. Best graphics card: AMD Radeon RX 9070.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Infinity Nikki is making headlines with its latest controversy about including Maye Musk in their 3.0 introductory trailer for Chinese players, but it seems that there are actually great surprises, according to other livestreams.

    Today, in the main dev livestream for Chinese players (translated by YouTuber Whimsy Haven in English), which is where most things are revealed before the patch actually drops.

    In the Infinity Nikki universe, people are coming up with theories and release schedules, where we are all travelling to next, and what the next abilities are.

    With Grand Theft Auto 6 grabbing everyone’s attention, it seems like a genius nod that the cosy styling game decided to show its claws and add guns to the mix.

    Nikki, in all her infinite universes and extended lore, is no stranger to guns, but so far it has been discussed heavily by fans whether Infold would take a safer approach and not give Nikki guns in the latest game.

    Thankfully for all lovers of shooters, that is not the case. Nikki already has a huge backdrop of dark lore, and it only makes sense that they would dim the vibes in-game even further with the addition of guns to use against foes and Esselings.

    The addition of a pink Barbie-esque convertible makes the Grand Theft Auto comparisons even funnier for fans of both, as we are all consumed by the hype for the Rockstar instant classic.

    Industry observers note that unlike Rockstar, Infinity Nikki fans also got a glimpse of her dancing with a new character, which looked very suspiciously like Oscar from Rose of Versailles. Some fans are taking it as a further nod to the queer fans and those locked into Nikki lore, where rumours of her sexuality have floated from the early games.

    But of course, the main star of the show is Nikki and the new character using guns. Now, with her new 'gal pal,' you can switch guns on the go as you fight foes, from a semi-automatic pistol to a short-barreled shotgun, as shown in the livestream.

    This is not the first gun in Infinity Nikki, as in 2.4 Nikki had a hunting shotgun which would only show up when the ability was used and wasn’t as flexible, leaving many fans disappointed but hopeful for more guns further on.

    Infinity Nikki fans also got a glimpse of dancing with a upcoming character, which looked very suspiciously like Oscar from Rose of Versailles.

    The other upcoming weapons seem to be wizard staffs, as we have already had a few wands in accessories rather than actual weapons, which makes sense in a game with a heavy dress-up mechanic.

    According to recent reports, the controversy with Maye Musk, Elon Musk’s mother, certainly put a dent in Infinity Nikki’s reputation, and the conversation between fans and devs has been strained. Nikki and her games are no strangers to controversy, and with the latest fiasco with Love and Deep Space still ongoing about Valko, only time will tell how Infold will react to all the communication between them and fans.

    Infold has generally been receptive to Infinity Nikki fans, who have been asking for guns, darker storylines, more romance (even if only hinted at), among other things.

    Sadly, we’re not sure if you can do drive-by shooting Grand Theft Auto style yet, as the footage of the car mostly focused on the streets of Cicia, but knowing Nikki and how you can summon the unicorn, bike, or motorcycle in different areas, the car should be able to breeze through weird forest terrain.

    It may make sense to ask for drive-by shooting mechanics in the next questionnaires for more fun updates, as the devs do listen to what the fans want to see next.

    All in all, interesting things are happening in the next massive Infinity Nikki update! No mention of poor Giovanni, though; he’s still in the basement.

    Infinity Nikki is available on PC, macOS, PlayStation 5, and iOS and Android phones.

    Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

    According to recent reports, as his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

    In a recent development, cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

    Sources indicate that cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” claims game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

    In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

    Mega Man: Dual Override introduces in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

    Police in Shanghai, China have reportedly arrested 13 people in connection with an alleged criminal scheme selling counterfeit Final Fantasy 7 figures.

    First reported by local Shanghai-based publication Shangguan News (translation via Automaton), in May Shanghai police began receiving complaints about Final Fantasy 7 Tifa Lockhart figures purchased from an online store that didn't match-up with the official toys licensed by rights holder Square Enix. Police reportedly verified with Square Enix that the seller had not been authorized to sell the figures, which appear to be nearly identical to an official Square Enix product, although seemingly without the articulation points that allow you to change the position of arms and legs. Here's a comparison via Dexerto's Twitter account:.

    Police have arrested 13 people accused of selling counterfeit Final Fantasy 7 Tifa Lockhart figures The Chinese sellers reportedly charged higher prices by including extra faces, hands, and accessories not found with the official figures https://t.co/AE1IyS0wi9November 19, 2026.

    Shanghai police have reportedly busted more than 30 similar cases of counterfeit figures or figurines in 2026 alone, resulting in more than 140 arrests and 70 million yuan, or $10.5 million, in seized assets.

    Final Fantasy 7 Revelation boss says the story isn't being "shaped by fan reactions," but the devs are using feedback on "the overall gameplay experience".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

    Sources indicate that unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

    It has been revealed that as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the substantial focus of this enhancement, in case it wasn't obvious.

    It has been revealed that the event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

    Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

    The hot newly introduced arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this upgrade. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

    Industry observers note that in combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

    Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

    If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

    In a recent development, returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

    Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a latest activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today.
    • You can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site.
    • It has been revealed that here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today. The full draft text of the regulation leaked earlier in the week. If it passes into law - and there's plenty of debate and revision ahead - it'll have significant consequences for the developers and publishers of games like Overwatch, Dota 2, and GTA Online.

    You can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site. The organisers have also published an introductory explainer that takes us through the timeline of the Act's gestation, dating back to 2020, and summarises its provisions. If passed, the Act will apply to any company doing business in the EU, not just those based in member states, with individual governments able to impose fines and consumers able to seek financial compensation if they think they've been harmed.

    It has been revealed that here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text. The Act proposes a number of provisions regarding "unfair" commercial practices, including omission and distortion in advertising and PR communication at large. Amongst other things, it takes aim at "dark patterns" – that is, "visual, auditory and other components" of online interfaces that are designed to manipulate or deceive. The text also forbids personalised advertising and pricing aimed at children, and prohibits influencers from making "direct exhortations to minors to buy products or to persuade their parents or other adults to buy products in commercial communications".

    The items that are probably of greatest interest to us smelly gamers are the passages on virtual currencies, "variable reward systems", and addictive design.

    The Act would require game publishers who sell virtual currencies to indicate the real-world monetary value of the currency and anything bought with it. It would also require companies to disable paid-for virtual currencies by default for kids, unless a parent or guardian has given approval.

    As for paid-for "variable reward systems", aka "loot boxes", "surprise mechanics", "Schrödinger's Giftbombs" or however publishers may prefer to describe them, the Act would require companies to state the "types" of object they might cough up, together with the probability of obtaining them. It would also oblige publishers to disable paid-for "variable reward systems" for minors, and give everybody an "easily accessible" way to switch them off.

    The draft Act outright prohibits "pay-to-progress and pay-to-win mechanisms" for kids. More generally, it suggests further constraints for publishers and developers who "design, organise or operate their digital products in a manner that is intended, or can reasonably be foreseen to encourage compulsive or excessive use". Again, it wants companies to give people options to switch these features off.

    That includes "features enabling automatic play of content and uninterrupted content consumption without effective and regular interruption moments that enable deliberation by the consumer on their willingness to consume more content". Also, "notifications not triggered by, or not directly related to, the consumer’s interaction or activity on the service", "features incentivising engagement at regular times or with greater frequency, including through penalties or loss of benefits", and "features and system behaviours that encourage continued use by simulating interpersonal relations," such as nagging prompts.

    If you'd like a more 'expert' account of the Digital Fairness Act - how dare you! I have read several Wikipedia pages - the bespectacled nabobs of GamesIndustry.biz went and got notes from an actual lawyer. All this follows a change in EU rating law last month aimed at safeguarding the weans from predatory habit-forming devices and instruments of financialisation - games with lootboxes are now PEGI 16 by default, while blockchain games are always rated 18. Across the pond, meanwhile, lawsuits are underway in Upcoming York and Washington against Valve's tolerance of lootboxes on Steam, which the lawyers in question define as illegal gambling.

    10 Best Metroidvania Boss Fights of the 2020s (So Far)

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Modern Metroidvanias, largely influenced by Soulsborne titles' formula, have heavily emphasized boss fights as the core of their gameplay, and I'm quite happy about it.
    • I can't deny my absolute fascination with formidable adversaries that test my reflexes, adaptability, and resolve, and this genre in particular has understood those keys better than most.
    • With each passing year, we not only receive more outstanding Metroidvanias but also specifically more experiences that utilize this gameplay concept to its fullest potential, usually representing the high points of their respective adventures.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Modern Metroidvanias, largely influenced by Soulsborne titles' formula, have heavily emphasized boss fights as the core of their gameplay, and I'm quite happy about it.

    I can't deny my absolute fascination with formidable adversaries that test my reflexes, adaptability, and resolve, and this genre in particular has understood those keys better than most.

    With each passing year, we not only receive more outstanding Metroidvanias but also specifically more experiences that utilize this gameplay concept to its fullest potential, usually representing the high points of their respective adventures.

    Therefore, if you're like me and fascinated by a good duel with health bars and numerous phases, I invite you to read this list of the ten best Metroidvania boss fights of the 2020s (so far).

    Well Dweller is a magnificent video game that, as the pinnacle of Kyle Thompson's craft, is brimming with spectacular yet accessible special bosses, such as The Queen.

    The plethora of sequences, attacks, and projectiles that unfold during your final encounter is breathtaking, truly connecting with the idea that royalty rules with an iron fist because they actually possess the power to dominate others.

    Disfiguring the face of your family's kidnapper is fitting for a title that's cozy on the surface but profoundly dark beneath it, materialized in a demanding fight in terms of positioning and movement that makes you feel like you're constantly swimming against the tide.

    While the bosses in Well Dweller wouldn't be my primary reason for recommending this gem, The Queen, in particular, demonstrates the wide variety that Metroidvanias can offer, rather than simply reducing everything to dodging and attacking in between.

    The entirety of Shinobi: Art of Vengeance is a moving marvel with choreography worthy of the best action sequences of recent years, thanks to the tremendous animations and magnificent display of audiovisual effects for bosses like Lord Ruse.

    Its imposing arena and visual design provide the perfect backdrop to prepare you for the epic duel this tormented villain has in store, whose tragic origin story is only surpassed by the way his darkness permeates the fight.

    What was once an honorable man surrenders his body and mind to an abject power that threatens the balance of the world, making it fitting that his fight resembles that of a ninja against a natural phenomenon capable of defying the laws of physics.

    The gameplay is very satisfying, forcing you to use all the tools and combos at your disposal to evade and attack effectively, leveraging the title's glorious combat system, where, after dominating all the combos, you can truly perform a martial aesthetic feast.

    The gimmick of having you constantly face a boss throughout a game is quite difficult to pull off successfully, but Gilroy, the Administrator from Ender Magnolia: Bloom in the Mist is a perfect example of when it's done well.

    While the game's roster of bosses is quite varied, its developers understand the magic of fighting a humanoid adversary who, true to FromSoftware's philosophy, forces you to decipher a rapid and relentless attack pattern where the slightest mistake is punished with death.

    Gilroy is a challenge that evolves in each of the three encounters, always leaving room for more secrets, until the final confrontation arrives with the full weight of the narrative, where you must fight one last battle that is as bittersweet as it is satisfying.

    Ender Magnolia is a game that relies heavily on its aesthetics, story, and music to amplify its emotional impact, so the campaign reaches its peak when you must defeat this recurring and memorable figure one last time.

    Speaking of recurring tropes throughout video game history, Tunic presents The Heir as the final boss very early in the story, allowing you to become familiar with its power while simultaneously understanding how far you are from completing your journey.

    Games with such a strong emphasis on exploration and adventure as this one must make every element contribute to the sense of progress, and nothing demonstrates your growth more than a superpowered entity with whom you gradually close the gap.

    Checking your evolution through repeated attempts over many hours is captivating, as is finally realizing you're on par and understanding the remarkable challenge it truly holds, hidden behind complex and rapid combos, diverse area attacks, and far more resistance than you initially expected.

    The Heir's fight is simple but makes the most of Tunic's functional mechanics, and the satisfaction of delivering the final blow after so many hours lost and disoriented is unparalleled.

    Ori and the Will of the Wisps constantly surpasses itself with each new boss, escape sequence, and scene, culminating in a Shriek encounter that ranges from breathtaking to utterly devastating.

    The franchise is a relentless litany of tragedies and victims that exact a toll on the kindness of those who suffer them, leading you to confront a majestic yet deeply traumatized owl amidst what appears to be the end of the universe.

    The screen seems to crumble as your confrontation with Shriek unfolds dynamically, with both combat and platforming sections taking place as the boss moves in and out of the frame with truly enviable dynamism.

    More than just a boss fight, the sequence feels like a genuine battle where a force of nature truly wants to defeat you; sensations enhanced by the magnificent soundtrack and the sheer madness of particles and colors displayed during the fight.

    Fighting Vahram in his godlike form inside the borders of time itself is among those images that stay with you forever, something Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown does quite regularly.

    These former brothers-in-arms clash in a magnificent duel where time freezes and reverses, beams of light and swords appear from all sides, and your adversary manipulates the laws of physics as if they were clay, making it a truly spectacular show.

    As you whittle down his health and he becomes cornered, the fight's complexity increases considerably, building to a tremendous crescendo where you feel the climax approaching and the adrenaline surging.

    Vahram is one of those bosses who can destroy you dozens of times in a row and you'll still be happy, because he's so well and precisely designed that each new opportunity to fight him again feels like a gift.

    True final bosses are usually the ultimate display of difficulty, depth, and passion that a Metroidvania has to offer, including Shii in MIO: Memories in Orbit.

    Fighting the companion who guided you throughout the story not because of some villainous adversity, but because of a genuine conflict of beliefs about what constitutes the most desirable outcome, is heartbreaking yet captivating, especially given the challenge that awaits.

    Shii lives up to his title, offering a multi-layered duel that demands you be as adept at recognizing openings as you are at dodging, jumping, dashing, grappling, flying, and more to evade its endless array of varied and omnidirectional attacks.

    The boss also flies, vanishes, glides, and crawls in an organic clash that makes the most of MIO: Memories in Orbit's environment and mechanics, resulting in an absolute delight.

    Blasphemous 2 boasts one of the most fluid and satisfying combat systems in the entire genre, but none exploit its flow state's sweet satisfaction quite like Eviterno, Last Desecrator.

    While the rest of the game is relatively manageable, this timeless warrior subverts expectations and delivers the beating of your life, proving that all the challenges you've overcome so far were just the tip of the iceberg he embodies.

    Far from the abominations and colossi you face during your crusade, the title presents, in its climax, a knight equal to you whose speed, power, and versatility demand pixel-perfect decision-making every second, regardless of your build.

    The best bosses are the ones that push you to your limits, and considering Eviterno penalizes even a millisecond off-timing or being a pixel too close, he's a clear contender for the decade's finest.

    Eigong is a mentor to our protagonist in Nine Sols both in story and gameplay, as no other encounter teaches you to appreciate its prodigious combat system so profoundly.

    There are fierce contenders throughout the campaign, though the one tasked with opposing Yi at the very end exponentially raises the demands of mechanical control, as any performance less than perfect will result in the same outcome: a return to the checkpoint.

    With three hellish phases brimming with rapid and agile movements—horizontal and vertical, parryable and unparryable, close and long range—it's an unstoppable barrage of abilities unless you know Yi's powers like the back of your hand.

    Only absolute, unwavering concentration will give you a chance against Eigong, whose defeat promptly transforms from a painful climb into one of the most magical memories a Metroidvania has ever offered.

    Being the only one on the entire list who isn't the game's final boss, which already hints at her unparalleled quality, Skarrsinger Karmelita is Hollow Knight: Silksong's highest point.

    That Team Cherry's masterpiece has the genre's best boss this decade is undeniable, with representatives like Trobbio, Second Sentinel, Cogwork Dancers, and Lace to justify it, but ultimately it's the queen of the ants who gets the recognition.

    It's a majestic encounter from the very beginning, leading you through the halls of a theater with her glorious singing, and then, after gifting you her minions as an offering to start the fight with full silk, appearing on stage to give you the concert of your life.

    The song, setting, art direction, attacks, rhythm, duration... Everything is perfectly timed to ensure a flawless experience, whether it takes you one try or a thousand (which is more likely).

    Skarrsinger Karmelita, I dare say, is among the best bosses in video game history and a perfect example of why this gameplay concept has gained so much relevance over the years.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

    As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

    Recent findings suggest that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the tech giant's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

    Recent findings suggest that this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

    Sources indicate that last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

    In a recent development, what do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

    Will a Grand Theft Auto game ever be set outside of America? Rockstar offers a small glimmer of hope

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (370 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, the Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being.
    • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami.
    • In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then quickly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

    Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

    In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then quickly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

    This is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when organization co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He remarked it was because cities like Miami and New York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

    There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

    Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

    According to recent reports, while discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij stated. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it.".

    GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans!
    • Black Forest, based in Germany, confirmed the move in a press release.
    • "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," added Third Signal founder Andreas Tobler.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans! remakes, have spun out of Embracer Group-owned publishers THQ Nordic via a management buyout and unveiled plans to form a new "developer-driven group" of independent studios. The new group, dubbed Third Signal, will aim to "give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom" to "bring their own ideas to life".

    Black Forest, based in Germany, confirmed the move in a press release. "We are grateful to THQ Nordic and Embracer for nine good years and the games we made together," co-boss Adrian Goersch stated. "Now, we're excited to shape our own future as owners again, to work on an exciting latest project with a great team and strong partners behind us.".

    "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," added Third Signal founder Andreas Tobler. "Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life." As of writing, Third Signal's website is just a logo splash which promises something coming soon. To be fair, it does also look to have an email address, plus legal and privacy notices. Black Forest's management team will become a co-owner of the studio group as part of this move, but "continue to collaborate on game development tasks" with THQ Nordic.

    In a recent development, black Forest had been in the embrace since 2017, releasing both 2020's Destroy All Humans! remake and Destroy All Humans! 2: Reprobed in that time, plus DLC Clone Carnage. Over the years they've also made multiple entries in the Giana Sisters platformer series, survival game Fade to Silence, and 2017's Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back.

    It has been revealed that that's a right old mix of stuff, but the biggest names in it are all resurrections of series or characters created by other folks back in the day. Pandemic Studios in the case of Destroy All Humans!, Accolade in the case of Bubsy, and Germany organization Time Warp in the case of Giana Sisters. That makes the fact it sounds like this move'll give Black Forest a bit more creative freedom intriguing. Here's hoping that if they do plan to try and get some more of their own original ideas off the ground, rather than trucking on with a steady diet of remakes and revivals, they manage to stick the landing. It's all fine declaring that a 50 person team can make a top game these days, but that certainly doesn't mean it's in any way easy to pull off.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

    This next major update arrives March 24, adding two newly introduced Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

    According to recent reports, most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some substantial rewards and earn glory.

    Sources indicate that among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

    Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier swiftly.

    Industry observers note that our first latest arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

    Sources indicate that when she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

    Industry observers note that the other fresh Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

    Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

    Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

    In a recent development, outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings upcoming themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

    Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

    Paradox boss Frederik Wester stepping down after several tumultuous years for the Cities Skylines and Stellaris publisher

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (623 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the manufacturer.
    • According to recent reports, in a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox remarked Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027.
    • "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester stated of his decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the manufacturer. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

    According to recent reports, in a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox remarked Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

    "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester stated of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My plan was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the tech giant's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

    It has been revealed that wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the company in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally launched last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox revealed a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

    It has been revealed that wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a fresh studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

    Despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

    Paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

    #86724. There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?

    📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1917 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

    There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1917 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price.
    • Sources indicate that in 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves.
    • Recent findings suggest that but the Nvidia of the late 1990s and early 2000s was a far cry from the vast (if tarnished) juggernaut it is today, and at the time it wasn’t even the obvious survivor.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price. It was choosing the right one among a glut of potential, reasonably affordable options.

    Sources indicate that in 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. Just two years later, at the turn of the newly introduced millennium, only 15 remained, and not long after that, there were merely two: Nvidia and ATI, nowadays part of AMD.

    Recent findings suggest that but the Nvidia of the late 1990s and early 2000s was a far cry from the vast (if tarnished) juggernaut it is today, and at the time it wasn’t even the obvious survivor. Research firm 4th Wave put ATI top for 1998 with 24.5 million 3D chips sold, followed by S3 with 15.2 million and Intel, in its first year in the market, with 6.5 million. Nvidia came fourth on 6.4 million. 3dfx, the tech giant whose Voodoo cards had made 3D gaming on PC a thing in the first place, sold 5.2 million.

    Each of those companies went under or sold up for one reason or another, but what’s striking is how most did so within a few years of one another. In the four years between 1998 and 2002, the graphics business essentially stopped rewarding whoever had the fastest chip, instead favouring the companies that could iterate the fastest. A fresh chip every six months or so for the same APIs everyone used, backed by enough capital to ride out the dot-com crash. Nvidia was built for that; almost nobody else was.

    The first companies to go didn’t need any help from Nvidia, though. 3D acceleration had made the humble graphics chip a much bigger and more expensive thing to design, and plenty of incumbents that had found their footing on 2D couldn’t afford to keep going. Tseng Labs stopped developing graphics chips at the end of 1997 with roughly $28 million still in the bank, selling its graphics engineers to ATI for about $3 million. Rendition, maker of the Vérité V1000 3D accelerator, agreed to sell itself to memory maker Micron in June 1998, and ATI bought Chromatic Research for $67 million that October.

    In its prospectus for its January 1999 IPO, Nvidia warned that PC makers brought out upcoming systems as often as twice a year, on a spring and fall schedule, and that missing one was a serious risk. The company subsequently reorganised itself around that schedule, releasing the GeForce 256 in October 1999 and the GeForce 3 in February 2001. By 2002, Nvidia’s annual report disclosed that separate design teams were working on several generations of chips at once.

    By this point, though, the writing had been on the wall for quite some time. S3, then the world’s second-largest graphics chip maker, wrote in its annual report for 1999 that a graphics chip stayed on sale for 12 to 18 months, and that a delay "as short as a few months" could cost it a design win with a PC maker. Any company that was rolling out just one major chip per year was launching against a rival’s refresh at best. At worst, it was launching late against next-gen chips.

    Sources indicate that that’s essentially what happened to 3dfx when Rampage, the chip that was meant to succeed the Voodoo5, never shipped. The company lost its other significant advantage around the same time with Glide, its own programming interface that only ran on Voodoo cards. Glide flourished while Direct3D, Microsoft’s rival interface built into Windows, was still lacking features, meaning that plenty of games ran best on 3dfx hardware, but that lead was rapidly eroded once Direct3D and rivals’ OpenGL drivers caught up; developers could now write a game once and run it on anyone’s card. By 1999, Creative was selling Nvidia-based Riva TNT cards with drivers that let Glide games run on them. 3dfx sued, then open-sourced Glide altogether that December.

    Sources indicate that by then, though, 3dfx had already made its most damaging mistake. A year earlier, on December 14, 1998, it agreed to buy graphics card maker STB Systems for about $141 million in stock, and CEO Greg Ballard remarked the Voodoo3 would only be sold on 3dfx’s cards. That revelation left Diamond and Creative in a tough spot, having built their gaming lines on Voodoo chips. They were now stuck high and dry without access to the new one.

    Sources indicate that 3dfx was solely concerned with its margins here. The price of its single-chip Voodoo Banshee card dropped from $150 to $89 within a month of launch. With prices in freefall, selling the finished Voodoo Banshee meant that 3dfx pocketed the margin that’d otherwise go to a partner like Diamond or Creative. Those boardmakers inevitably walked, and went where the chips were. STB had been selling Nvidia cards right up to the deal, and its last annual report includes a $3 million note it held from "Nvidia Corporation, a supplier." Creative already had Riva TNT cards on shelves, and Nvidia, which then didn’t make its own cards, would sell its chips to anyone.

    In a recent development, intel, meanwhile, was causing problems from the other end of the market. Its i740 "Auburn" graphics chip introduced in early 1998, and Microprocessor Report, the newsletter for the industry’s engineers, argued that Intel’s arrival encouraged Cirrus Logic, Oak and others to fold that year. Just over a year later, after lacklustre sales, Intel confirmed that it was ending support for the i740, then pulled out of standalone desktop graphics chips altogether to put graphics into its motherboard chipsets instead, starting with the i810. This was extremely problematic for companies like S3, Trident, and SiS. They survived on cheap chips for massive PC makers, and by the second half of 2001, estimates say Intel’s integrated graphics business had risen to control 55% of the market. That, in turn, pushed S3 to sell its graphics business to a VIA joint venture for $323 million.

    Then the money ran out. Venture funding for graphics startups had already dried up in 1999 as the dot-com bubble deflated, and exits inevitably followed. 3dfx lost $100.5 million in the second quarter of 2000, with its CEO blaming a late Voodoo5, and on December 15 that year it sold its assets to Nvidia for $70 million in cash (and a million Nvidia shares) after failing to secure credit. STMicroelectronics, which made the PowerVR-based Kyro II, quit PC graphics in early 2002.

    In a recent development, ATI, however, survived alongside Nvidia because it was already operating in the way the newly introduced market wanted it to. It was the biggest seller at the time, and it made its own graphics cards, which Microprocessor Report mentioned brought in most of its revenue and margin. So, making its own cards wasn’t 3dfx’s mistake; it was locking out boardmakers who had been selling Voodoo cards for it. That pushed those boardmakers towards Nvidia, and a late Voodoo5 and cash crunch dealt the death blow. ATI also used its stock to buy the engineers that its rivals were shedding: Tseng’s, Chromatic’s, then, in February 2000, ArtX’s for $400 million, a team that’d just designed the Flipper graphics chip for Nintendo’s GameCube.

    For the next two decades, the the graphics industry was dominated by ATI - which eventually folded into AMD in 2006 - and Nvidia. For a while, it was a real fight. AMD paid $5.4 billion for ATI, and in the second quarter of 2010, Radeon cards briefly overtook Nvidia in discrete graphics shipments. However, AMD had a problem: it couldn’t really afford ATI. It wrote off $1.6 billion of goodwill from the deal about a year after it closed, and its PC chip business kept struggling.

    According to recent reports, by early 2015, AMD’s CPU and GPU revenue was down 38% on the year, and the firm was close to negative book value. Its quarterly R&D budget had fallen to its lowest level since 2004, with Nvidia spending nearly half as much again. Radeon cards stayed on the same Graphics Core Next architecture for about seven years before RDNA arrived in 2019. By then, Nvidia had already debuted its RTX cards with dedicated ray tracing hardware and Tensor cores for AI, and it never gave that lead back.

    According to recent reports, intel was the only company with pockets deep enough to try breaking back in. Its first go, Larrabee, was cancelled as a consumer graphics chip in December 2009. It finally got there in 2022, when the Arc A770 went on sale from $329, alongside the cheaper A750. Both arrived after repeated delays and struggled with older DirectX 9 games, and many observers - RPS included - put their chances of breaking up the Nvidia-AMD duopoly at low. By the time then-hardware editor James returned to the A750 in 2023, Intel had drastically improved its drivers, bringing significant gains to both general performance and DX9 compatibility. Even then, the Arc series had yet to prove it could work well at launch, without the need to be ironed out across months of updates.

    The second generation did indeed fare better, with the Arc B580 successfully selling out at $249 in December 2024. But that still barely impacted the wider industry, with Intel sitting at just 1% of graphics card shipments in the third quarter of 2025 and around 2% this spring, when Nvidia took roughly 90% of the 12.5 million cards shipped.

    Industry observers note that it now looks like Intel is on its way back out of gaming graphics cards. In April, leaker Jaykihn claimed that its next-generation Celestial gaming cards had been cancelled "long ago," and the latest rumours say B580 supply could be cut so Intel can sell more Arc Pro cards for, surprise surprise, AI work. It’s key to note that Intel hasn’t confirmed any of that, and one of its execs has remarked that Arc isn’t leaving its PC roadmap. Still, Intel had everything 3dfx didn’t: the cash, the PC makers on side, and the same APIs as everyone else. But money can’t buy two decades of Nvidia and AMD fixing their drivers game by game, and it seems to have decided its capital is better spent on AI anyway.

    Recent findings suggest that evidently, the question of where all the other GPU makers went does not have one single answer. Some couldn’t afford the rising costs, some couldn’t keep pace with a latest Nvidia chip every six months, and some lost their cheap business to Intel’s integrated graphics or went under when the dot-com bubble burst. Left over was a Nvidia/ATI (later AMD) duopoly, and PC gamers haven’t exactly done well out of it. We saw the RTX 4080 launch at $1,199 in 2022, nearly twice the 3080’s price, and the ongoing, AI-driven RAM shortage has pushed prices higher still.

    Recent findings suggest that in 1998, 47 companies wanted your money. Now there are two, and the bigger one, Nvidia, sells nine of every 10 graphics cards - yet still makes most of its money from data centres. Eighteen years on, it's a bad time to be a PC gamer, and nobody’s in a hurry to make things any better.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Fortnite Treasure Hours are now live, running from 2-4pm ET (7-9pm GMT), and today is your last chance to get the Golden Hatsune Miku skin.
    • During the event, everyone spawns with The Leekcapper and a Self-Revive Device, and on top of the usual boosts, Fortune and Cursed Sprites appear more often.
    • Drop rates across the board are increased for the full two hours of the event, much like past weeks:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Fortnite Treasure Hours are now live, running from 2-4pm ET (7-9pm GMT), and today is your last chance to get the Golden Hatsune Miku skin.

    During the event, everyone spawns with The Leekcapper and a Self-Revive Device, and on top of the usual boosts, Fortune and Cursed Sprites appear more often.

    Drop rates across the board are increased for the full two hours of the event, much like past weeks:.

    It's worth noting that Epic Games teased when it first disclosed the odds that "these rates may be higher in future," so with GTA 6 now in everyone's hands and over half of all active console players taking a vacation to Leonida, maybe we'll be treated to better drop rates this time around. Though nothing has been announced yet.

    The second Treasure Hours session goes live at 9-11pm ET (2-4am GMT), though unfortunately, Epic Games has not responded to the growing frustration from European and Asian players, who are forced to stay up past midnight if they want better odds.

    In a recent development, in fact, the official French social channels for Fortnite mused last week that there would be another session between 3-5am "for the bravest," dismissing these concerns outright. It should go without saying, but don't stay up until 5am opening chests. Even with 2x odds, it's incredibly unlikely you'll get Pirate Shop Access.

    Sources indicate that for those in more reasonable time zones, you can look forward to increased odds in the second session, with a 10x boost to the Golden Cap'n Miku drop rate — who has become as much an obsession for her vocaloid fans as the Pirate Shop Access tokens this week. Though with a drop rate of 1 in 1.56 million, let's just say Golden Hatsune Miku is pretty rare, even with a 10x boost.

    According to recent reports, we'll keep this article updated if Epic Games reveals a special GTA 6 incentive or any other details for today's Treasure Hours, but otherwise, if you want Golden Hatsune Miku, you'd best get opening chests. Just don't stay up too late trying your luck.

    It has been revealed that survivor's coin flip remains a controversial addition to the game, as fans debate the pros and cons of what it brings to the CBS series. I initially didn't have concerns with what went down with Lewis Kelly in Season 51's flip, until I learned there was more than one flip involved.

    Lewis spoke to Rob Has A Podcast about his exit and was asked if he'd pick water over fire if he flipped the coin again in a future season. The third juror revealed that he didn't have to think about the hypothetical, because he flipped the coin twice the night of his elimination. Hear the story below:.

    Well, here's the thing. I did actually do it once [before the one shown] and it didn't land in the circle, and I hear 'fire.' And maybe I should've changed it. I didn't think about it, so, it's tough.

    Lewis had to flip the coin twice, and the first time it landed on fire! Unfortunately, because it didn't land primarily in the circle placed on the ground, it was negated and he had to flip it again. Lewis didn't say how he felt about that, but I can say that as a Survivor fan, I'm pissed.

    Survivor 51's Kilby Lost All Of His Worldly Possessions After A Wild Storage Wars Scheme Went South.

    I went back and watched Survivor, and Jeff Probst noted that the contestant who correctly called the coin flip won immunity, an idol, and the grand prize went up another million. The only rule was that it had to land on what he called. At no point was it said the coin had to land on the mat, which wasn't even used for the shot of Lewis' coin flip.

    According to recent reports, jeff's word is law on Survivor, and if he's allowed to push contestants to admit they like fire challenges on-camera, he should've honored the result of the initial coin flip. Obviously, they faked it for the camera that he took the flip a second time on camera. They should've stuck with his original flip result and just filmed until he recreated it in the way they wanted it shot.

    To me, multiple flips for the coin feel sketchy. Sure, Lewis had a 50/50 shot both times, and one flip didn't impact the outcome of the other. At the same time, Lewis won the first flip and had it negated by something that wasn't part of the rules. Is it then fair that his odds of survival went back to 50% for a redo?

    Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

    Now, there's also a third option here in which the mat and all of that was explained to Lewis ahead of the flip, and maybe that's why he wasn't as bent out of shape as I am. I'll also admit he was one of my favorites, so I'm also sad about seeing him head to the jury before this season wraps up on the 2026 TV schedule.

    Recent findings suggest that survivor's Open Era continues to be full of surprises, which certainly keeps both the contestants and viewers on their toes. I think the biggest disappointment with this coin flip is that the payoff was pushed to next season. Right now, all we have to fester on is disappointment, and the fact that someone threw away their chance to stay in the game on a coin flip. We'll see what happens next Wednesday, and how Lewis' exit will impact the group dynamic.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Developer FromSoftware has declared that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.
    • FromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server issue".
    • Recent findings suggest that fromSoftware never specified the exact glitch impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Developer FromSoftware has declared that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

    FromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server issue". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

    Recent findings suggest that fromSoftware never specified the exact glitch impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

    "We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

    Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

    Industry observers note that this isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

    In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently announced - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially introduced, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

    All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

    Recent findings suggest that it has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

    Industry observers note that the action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

    It has been revealed that indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

    Sources indicate that this peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

    Sources indicate that crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

    It has been revealed that on Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

    Sources indicate that if you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or proposal to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

    Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

    In the first case, at least, something is being done.

    According to recent reports, developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”.

    Industry observers note that today’s patch follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

    The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

    This latest upgrade only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

    Industry observers note that the most vital changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

    There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer mentioned we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

    Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

    If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added upcoming pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.
    • It has been revealed that the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CD Projekt Red has revealed that it used - and is using - generative AI technology to treat and alter the voice of the Polish actor who portrayed Geralt of Rivia in upcoming Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past.

    It has been revealed that the actor, Jacek Rozenek, has portrayed Geralt of Rivia in all the major Witcher games, meaning his voice has become as synonymous with the role in Poland as Doug Cockle's has for people playing in English. But Rozenek suffered a severe stroke in 2019 that left him temporarily unable to speak, and when he was able to talk and perform again, the tonality and quality of his voice had changed.

    It's for these reasons that CD Projekt Red - with Rozenek's consent - employed the help of a firm called Respeecher to alter the lines he recorded for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion using generative-AI technology. As confirmed to Game File, an AI trained on Rozenek's previous Witcher work is retreating his recordings to make them sound more like the Geralt you hear elsewhere in The Witcher 3.

    "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," Jacek Rozenek explained. "I have great trust ... for the creators of this game.".

    Sources indicate that game File heard both treated and untreated recordings of Rozenek's Songs of the Past work, and reported a "significant" difference between them. Rozenek's untreated voice was apparently "deep and gravelly" and "noticeably rougher than his recordings for the original game". But treated, the voice was "far smoother and sounds younger", and closer to the original Witcher 3 Geralt recordings.

    Industry observers note that this isn't the first time CD Projekt Red has used generative AI for voice recordings in one of its games. The studio worked with Respeecher in 2023 to produce latest voiceover lines for Cyberpunk 2077 expansion Phantom Liberty. Viktor Vektor actor Miłogost "Miłek" Reczek passed away in 2021, after the original game was released, and CD Projekt Red didn't want to recast the role. Reczek's sons apparently gave their blessing for their father's voice to be artificially generated.

    "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically with consent and also to do something good," CD Projekt Red localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed told Game File, referring to the Rozenek recordings.

    According to recent reports, "For future projects, when we consider Geralt is becoming older and has a deeper voice, this is not a problem for us at all. It's more about this specific situation here, where we have both the voice from 12 years ago and from now next to each other, which could kind of take people out of the experience and feel that there is this difference.".

    In a recent development, the third Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, releases at some point next year, an unprecedented 12 years after the original game introduced. It adds an entirely new region, Letten, and centres its main story around Geralt's missing bardic bestie Dandelion, whose family lives there.

    In preparation for the expansion, a remastered version of The Witcher 3 was released a couple of months ago, overhauling the old role-playing adventure and bringing its baseline presentation more in line with what we'd expect from a modern game; it also overhauled some animations and enemy behaviours and reworked skill trees. For that reason, old-gen consoles PS4 and Xbox One won't receive the Songs of the Past expansion, despite The Witcher 3 being available on them.
